items.title: [v3 docs] Restore usable article navigation on mobile and tablet
items.body:
## Problem

A reader-experience audit of the local `releases/v3.0.0` documentation at `18a9809b30ddd0303b1da22f4db12fc589e14ba6` found two related responsive navigation defects. This issue concerns usability, separate from the content-accuracy audit in #6337.

## Reproduction

1. Build with pinned M-Press 1.0.19 (`mpress build --strict --no-purge-css`) and serve `docs/mpress/site` as a static site.
2. Open `/quick-start/installation/` at a 390 × 844 CSS pixel viewport.
3. Click the apparent “On this page >” control. It does nothing: this is a `<strong>` element without a button role, keyboard focus, or disclosure behaviour. All `.toc > a` except `.active` have `display: none`, so there is no way to choose another section from the displayed table of contents.
4. Open the navigation menu. The fixed table-of-contents bar covers the top of the menu, including most of “Home”. At this viewport Home is at y=80..112 and the TOC spans y=58..100. `document.elementsFromPoint(50,96)` returns the TOC above Home.

The same active-only TOC pattern applies at the <=1050px breakpoint. The menu overlap was reproduced at 390px. Source: `docs/mpress/custom.css`, responsive TOC rules around lines 300–342. The menu starts at y=64 while the mobile header is 58px high.

## Reader impact

Readers on smaller screens lose the ability to jump through a long article and encounter an apparent control that cannot be operated. Opening site navigation leaves the article TOC on top of the menu. Desktop articles otherwise have useful full TOCs.

## Scope and acceptance criteria

- Provide an actual section chooser at mobile/tablet breakpoints, using a semantic disclosure/button or another keyboard-operable pattern.
- Show all applicable article sections when expanded and make selection scroll to the correct heading without hiding it behind fixed headers.
- Keep the article TOC behind/hidden while site navigation is open; Home must be fully visible and clickable.
- Verify 390×844, a tablet width within 721–1050px, desktop, keyboard focus, and light/dark themes.
- Keep existing navigation and desktop TOC behaviour working.

Severity: P2, documentation UI bug. Prioritise as a bug fix outside the feature-only v3.1.0 milestone/project. No implementation or push was performed by this audit.

## Wider assessment context

The onboarding sequence is clear and desktop pages are readable. Further improvements worth evaluating: simplify the many equally prominent sidebar categories; make Next Steps a guided progression; move the Windows Dev Drive optimisation tip below the first working-app milestone; and reduce search ambiguity. Current search reproductions: `CLI` returns two identical “CLI Reference” titles/descriptions (`/guides/cli/` and `/reference/cli/`, already related to #6337 consolidation); `call Go from JavaScript` places Method Bindings seventh, behind migration, a beta blog post, and contributor internals. `system tray` and `open file` return the expected feature first. These ranking and information-architecture recommendations are expert-review observations, not measured first-time-user study results.

Audit used a fresh local build and current screenshots in isolated Chromium at 1440×1000 and 390×844. Search Enter navigation, theme switching, platform-tab synchronisation, and the reading-settings panel were exercised. No production deployment, external search-engine discovery, screen reader, touch hardware, or network performance claims are made.

items.title: macOS: Fn/Globe key (keyCode 63) swallowed by WKWebView before reaching IME — IME voice shortcuts fail in Wails apps

milestone.title: Future
milestone.description: Unscheduled feature work beyond GA. Placement here is not a commitment to a specific release. Goose should move items to a numbered milestone only when that release scope is justified.

items.body:
## Summary

On macOS, the **Fn / Globe key (`keyCode 63`) is swallowed by WKWebView before it ever reaches the input method**, so any IME feature triggered by holding Fn (e.g. voice input / push-to-talk shortcuts in Chinese input methods like 豆包输入法/DoubaoIme) silently fails **inside every Wails app window**, while the same IME works fine in native apps and Chromium apps.

## Environment

- macOS 26.2, Apple Silicon (arm64)
- Wails app: Reasonix Desktop (Wails/WKWebView variant, v1.31.4, `com.wails.reasonix-desktop`) — but this affects **any** Wails app on macOS
- IME: DoubaoIme (豆包输入法), voice shortcut bound to "hold Fn/Globe"

## Observed behavior

| Target | Pressing Fn (physical or remapped) while IME voice input is active |
|---|---|
| Native app (e.g. TextEdit, SwiftUI app) | ✅ IME receives the key, voice input starts |
| Chromium app (Chrome, Codex desktop) | ✅ works |
| **Wails app (WKWebView)** | ❌ IME never receives it — no reaction at all |

Typing in the Wails app works fine (`keyDown` path → `NSTextInputContext` → IME). The problem is specific to the **bare Fn modifier event**: it arrives as `flagsChanged` and is dropped.

## Root cause (upstream WebKit)

WebKit's `WebViewImpl::flagsChanged()` explicitly filters `keyCode 63` (Fn/Globe) and returns **before** calling `interpretKeyEvent()` (the call that hands the event to the current `NSTextInputContext` / IME):

- https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/main/Source/WebKit/UIProcess/mac/WebViewImpl.mm#L5916-L5920
- https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/main/Source/WebKit/UIProcess/mac/WebViewImpl.mm#L6826-L6840

Chinese IMEs commonly use "hold Fn/Globe to speak" as a voice shortcut, and hardware remappers (e.g. turning a Bluetooth remote's mic button into Fn) produce exactly this event, so both physical and remapped Fn fail.

## Request

Please consider a macOS-side fix in Wails so Fn/Globe events are forwarded to the input context instead of being silently dropped, e.g. install a `NSEventMaskFlagsChanged` local monitor on the Wails window that, for `keyCode 63`, forwards the event to the current first responder's `[inputContext handleEvent:event]` while still passing the original event through to AppKit (per Apple's `NSTextInputContext.handleEvent` docs: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nstextinputcontext/handleevent(_:)).

A WebKit-upstream fix would be "deliver Fn to the IME while still not generating a DOM keyboard event".

## Minimal repro

1. Install any Chinese IME that supports a "hold Fn to speak" voice shortcut (e.g. DoubaoIme) and bind its voice key to Fn/Globe.
2. Open any Wails app, focus a text field, and make sure the IME is active.
3. Hold Fn and speak → nothing happens.
4. Repeat in TextEdit or Chrome → works.

## Related

- Wails v3 Chinese-input issues (closed, different symptom): #4550, #2933

items.body:
### Description

### Application Window Receives Focus
- When the application window gains focus, the embedded WebView does not automatically receive focus. The only way to interact with the WebView is by clicking inside it. This issue occurs after launching the application and switching to it using `Alt+Tab` or by clicking on the title bar.
- Elements within the WebView don't receive focus as expected:
	- If a JavaScript function attempts to focus an element when the DOM is ready or the document is focused, that element does not receive focus. Use cases are using React `useEffect` or Svelte `onMount`, or subscribing to the document `onfocus` event.

### Tab Cycling (Pressing the Tab Key)
- When the application window has focus, pressing `Tab` does not move the focus to the WebView.
- When the WebView has focus, pressing `Tab` does not cycle focus out to the application window.

The issues described below occur in both Wails v2.9.0 and v3.0.0-alpha.7

### To Reproduce


### Wails v2

1. Create and launch a new Wails v2 application:
   ```
   wails init -n myfirstapp-wails2
   cd myfirstapp-wails2
   wails dev
   ```
2. Follow the steps below.

### Wails v3

1. Create and launch a new Wails v3 application:
   ```
   wails3 init -n myfirstapp-wails3
   cd myfirstapp-wails3
   wails3 dev
   ```
2. Follow the steps below.

### Steps

#### Focus Issue
1. Click inside an input field within the WebView.
2. Switch to another application so that the Wails app loses focus.
3. Switch back to the Wails application using one of the following methods:
   - Use `Alt+Tab`
   - Click the application icon in the taskbar
   - Click the title bar
4. **Issue:** 
   - The input field does not regain focus.
   - Pressing `Tab` does not bring focus to the WebView or the input field.
   - Focus appears to be stuck on the application’s title bar.

#### Tab Cycling Issue
1. Click inside an input field within the WebView.
2. Press the `Tab` key.
3. Focus moves to the "Greet" button.
4. Press `Tab` again.
5. **Issue:**
   - Focus cycles back to the input field.
   - The application’s title bar never receives focus while the WebView has focus.
   - Pressing `Tab` repeatedly only cycles through focusable elements within the WebView.

### Expected behaviour

### Expected Behavior
- The WebView or the last focused element should receive focus when the application window gains focus (via `Alt+Tab` or clicking on the title bar).
- Pressing `Tab` should cycle through all focusable elements, including both the WebView and the application window (title bar and other controls).

### Actual Behavior
- The WebView does not gain focus unless explicitly clicked after the application window gains focus.
- The `Tab` key only cycles through elements inside the WebView and never reaches the application window (title bar or other controls).
- WebView focus is stuck within the WebView's DOM elements and does not extend to the application title bar.

### Behavior on Linux / Windows WSL

On Ubuntu, the behavior differs slightly:
- When the window is created, `Tab` can be used to navigate through focusable elements within the WebView.
- The last focused element retains focus after switching between applications.
- Tab cycling includes both WebView elements and the window's title bar.

items.body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

_No response_

### Describe the solution you'd like

The idea is to have a component like `WebviewWindow` (i called it `WebviewPanel`) which automatically inherits every functionality of `WebviewWindow` and behaves like a floating window / overlay (depending on the OS).

### Describe alternatives you've considered

I have found a solution which uses Go's struct embedding to extend `WebviewWindow` so that there is no need to touch the objective-c bindings or care about porting any change made on `WebviewWindow` to `WebviewPanel`. This is true also for the `WindowOptions`.
However my implementation, for now, supports only MacOS NSPanel.

My implementation was first created from version `v3.0.0-alpha.6`, and after the `v3.0.0-alpha.7` new version, I have already made a merge with the new changes. The repo is at https://github.com/nixpare/wails/tree/v3-alpha-feature/mac-panel.

You can test a working example from my repo https://github.com/nixpare/wails-mac-panel, the PR version of wails is already vendored in the code, so just `wails3 dev` is needed.

### Additional context

### Important notes on changes i made:
- `application.App` key bindings callback function now has `application.Window` as the argument and not `*application.WebviewWindow`
- the Objective-C `WebviewWindow` interface, instead of extending `NSWindow` directly, uses composition and now has a property for the reference to the window, which could be both a `NSWindow` or a `NSPanel`, so the keyboard events are now managed by `WebviewResponder`
- the C bindings that bridges the Objective-C code to Go were moved in a separate file

#### Additional small bugs encountered and fixes:
- Even after a `Window` is closed, some events are sent to the channel `windowEvents`, resulting in error logs printed in the console. I just have changed the log function to include the window event ID
- When sending the key combination `ctrl+m`, the first if statement in the Objective-C function `keyStringFromEvent` return `"enter"`, now the new `WebviewResponder` first interprets the `event.keyCode` and then as a special case the `event.characters` string
- When sending the key combination `ctrl+l`, this combination never reaches the application runtime, both in the "old" and "new" versions

items.title: Support Web MIDI API in Wails Desktop Apps
items.body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

The [Web MIDI API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Web_MIDI_API) is a suite of functionality that allows JavaScript to interface with a connected MIDI device. The entrance to this API is `navigator.requestMIDIAccess` which Wails Apps do not appear to support. Google Chrome supports it (as do some other, but not all other, browsers) but when running as a standalone desktop app, Wails' web engine does not appear to support it (verified using the console in a running wails app and checking for `navigator.requestMIDIAccess` which was `undefined`).


### Describe the solution you'd like

I would like for Wails to support the Web MIDI API and `navigator.requestMIDIAccess` so that I can run my application stand-alone without a browser as intended. I don't know what this involves to make this happen, but it's a real bummer that I have to run this through Chrome to make it work instead of standalone. Still, better that there is some solution than none.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

Running the application through Google Chrome which does support the Web MIDI API and `navigator.requestMIDIAccess` allows MIDI devices to connect and interface with JavaScript properly. I do not know if there is another way to interface with MIDI devices that is currently supported, but from what I have read, the Web MIDI API is the intended way.

### Additional context

I am working on a desktop application for training one's ability to read sheet music. It displays a musical note like what you would see on a piece of sheet music and prompts you to guess what it is. Your guess can be clicked, typed, or most importantly, _keyed in on a MIDI keyboard_.

My issue arises from how you set up a JavaScript application to read from a MIDI device. The current way you do that is through the Web MIDI API by invoking `navigator.requestMIDIAccess`. [Here is the spec](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Navigator/requestMIDIAccess) for that function. One thing to note is that it specifies that you must be in a secure context for it to be available, which you can check via `window.isSecureContext`. Running this in the Wails app console reports that it **is** a secure context, so if this function were supported it _would_ be available.

This function is supported in Google Chrome which I have been using to test my code since Wails lets you use a browser against localhost in addition to just the standalone application if you wish. When I check under Chrome's console for `navigator.requestMIDIAccess`, the console returns a valid and recognized function that the browser implements. If I do the same using the standalone app that gets spun up by Wails, it's console reports that `navigator.requestMIDIAccess` is `undefined`.

This isn't completely unprecedented, I also found that Mozilla Firefox does not support this function either ( apparently it is supported on nightly builds, just not the current stable release), and I am not sure if it's because it's new or experimental or anything like that, but it is worth noting that the Web MIDI API is also supported in more than just Google Chrome.

I don't know what the backing web engine is for Wails, I checked `navigator.userAgent` in Wails' console and it just reported that it's `wails.io`, which isn't terribly clear. So, if it's based on Firefox somehow, that may explain the lack of support for this function.

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

On macOS there is currently no way to create a Wails window that behaves like
an `NSPanel` with `NSWindowStyleMaskNonactivatingPanel`. Today, every Wails
window is a plain `NSWindow` whose `canBecomeKeyWindow` and
`canBecomeMainWindow` are hard-coded to `YES`, and `Show()` / `Focus()` call
`-[NSApplication activateIgnoringOtherApps:YES]` followed by
`makeKeyAndOrderFront:`.

That makes a few common macOS UI patterns impossible to build with Wails v3:

- Menu-bar / status-bar apps that pop a small detail panel without stealing
  focus from the app the user is currently typing in.
- Spotlight / Raycast / Alfred-style command bars that need to float above
  every Space (including fullscreen apps) and accept keyboard input without
  activating the host app.
- Floating tool palettes / inspectors next to a fullscreen document app
  (Sketch, Figma desktop, Final Cut, etc.).

The pieces needed to express "accessory app with a floating overlay" already
exist (`Mac.ActivationPolicy = ActivationPolicyAccessory`,
`Mac.WindowLevel = MacWindowLevelFloating`,
`MacWindowCollectionBehaviorCanJoinAllSpaces | …FullScreenAuxiliary`), but
without the panel style mask the window still grabs focus on click, which
defeats the whole pattern.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Add a `NonActivatingPanel bool` field to the `MacWindow` options struct in
`pkg/application/webview_window_options.go`, e.g.:

```go
// NonActivatingPanel makes the window an NSPanel with the
// NSWindowStyleMaskNonactivatingPanel style. Clicking or typing into the
// window will not activate the application or steal focus from the
// currently active app. Intended for tool palettes, floating overlays
// and menu-bar app detail panels. macOS only.
NonActivatingPanel bool
```

Implementation outline (all changes are confined to the existing darwin
files):

1. **`pkg/application/webview_window_darwin.h`** — change the `WebviewWindow`
   superclass from `NSWindow` to `NSPanel`. `NSPanel` is an `NSWindow`
   subclass so existing call sites are unaffected, but only `NSPanel`
   honors `NSWindowStyleMaskNonactivatingPanel`.

2. **`pkg/application/webview_window_darwin.go`** — extend the existing
   `windowNew(...)` C constructor with a `bool nonActivatingPanel`
   parameter and OR `NSWindowStyleMaskNonactivatingPanel` into the style
   mask when set.

3. **`pkg/application/webview_window_darwin.m`** — make
   `canBecomeKeyWindow` still return `YES` (so text fields work) but make
   `canBecomeMainWindow` return `NO` when the panel bit is set, which is
   the canonical AppKit pattern for accessory panels.

4. **`pkg/application/webview_window_darwin.go`** — branch `windowShow`
   and `windowFocus` so that, when the panel bit is present, they use
   `orderFrontRegardless` / `orderFront:` instead of
   `makeKeyAndOrderFront:` and skip the
   `[NSApp activateIgnoringOtherApps:YES]` call. Without this step the
   style bit alone has no visible effect because `Show()` still pulls
   focus.

5. **`(*macosWebviewWindow).run()`** — pass the new flag through from
   `options.Mac.NonActivatingPanel` to `C.windowNew`.

Example usage from a consuming app:

```go
app.NewWebviewWindowWithOptions(application.WebviewWindowOptions{
    Frameless: true,
    Mac: application.MacWindow{
        NonActivatingPanel: true,
        ActivationPolicy:   application.ActivationPolicyAccessory,
        WindowLevel:        application.MacWindowLevelFloating,
        CollectionBehavior: application.MacWindowCollectionBehaviorCanJoinAllSpaces |
                            application.MacWindowCollectionBehaviorFullScreenAuxiliary,
        Backdrop:           application.MacBackdropTranslucent,
    },
})
```

### Describe alternatives you've considered

- **Use only `WindowLevel: MacWindowLevelFloating` + `ActivationPolicyAccessory`.**
  This floats the window but still activates the Wails app on first click and
  steals focus from whatever the user was typing into. Not viable for
  Spotlight-/Raycast-style UIs.

- **Drop down to private CGS/Carbon APIs from a Go cgo wrapper in the
  consuming app.** Possible, but it requires duplicating Wails' window
  creation, breaks on every macOS update and forfeits the entire
  `WebviewWindow` lifecycle (events, dragging, drag-and-drop, content
  protection, liquid glass, etc.).

- **Run a separate helper process (e.g. a tiny Swift app) for the panel.**
  Solves the problem but doubles the binary, adds IPC, and is
  disproportionate given that AppKit already exposes the exact behavior
  via a single style-mask bit.

- **Toggle `[NSApp setActivationPolicy:Accessory]` plus
  `orderFrontRegardless` only.** Reduces the activation but the window
  still becomes key on click because `canBecomeMainWindow` returns `YES`,
  so the front app loses key-window status. The panel style mask is what
  AppKit specifically designed for this case.

### Additional context

- Reference: Apple docs for `NSWindowStyleMaskNonactivatingPanel`
  https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nswindow/stylemask-swift.struct/nonactivatingpanel
- Prior art in other webview frameworks:
  - Electron: `BrowserWindow({ type: 'panel' })` (sets the same style mask
    on macOS).
  - Tauri: `WindowBuilder::nonactivating_panel(true)` on macOS.
- The codebase already has the helper machinery this would compose with
  (`MacWindowLevel`, `MacWindowCollectionBehavior`, `ActivationPolicy`,
  `MacBackdropTranslucent`); only the style-mask bit and the
  `Show()`/`Focus()` activation call are missing.

items.title: [Feedback Wanted] Experimental GTK4 + WebKitGTK 6.0 Support
items.body:
> [!NOTE]
> **Status: Merged into `v3-alpha`**
>
> [PR #4958](https://github.com/wailsapp/wails/pull/4958) has been merged. Clone from `v3-alpha` to test this feature.

---

Wails v3 now includes **experimental** support for GTK4 and WebKitGTK 6.0 on Linux via the `-tags gtk4` build flag.

## Why GTK4?

- **Better Wayland support** - Native Wayland rendering without X11 compatibility layer
- **Improved performance** - GPU-accelerated rendering pipeline
- **Modern features** - Fractional scaling, HDR support, better HiDPI handling
- **Future-proof** - GTK3 is in maintenance mode, GTK4 is the future of Linux desktop

---

## Getting Started

### Step 1: Install System Dependencies

Install GTK4 and WebKitGTK 6.0 development packages:

| Distro | Command |
|--------|---------|
| **Ubuntu/Debian** | `sudo apt install libgtk-4-dev libwebkitgtk-6.0-dev` |
| **Fedora** | `sudo dnf install gtk4-devel webkitgtk6.0-devel` |
| **Arch Linux** | `sudo pacman -S gtk4 webkitgtk-6.0` |
| **openSUSE** | `sudo zypper install gtk4-devel webkitgtk-6_0-devel` |
| **Gentoo** | `sudo emerge gui-libs/gtk net-libs/webkit-gtk:6` |
| **Solus** | `sudo eopkg install libgtk-4-devel libwebkit-gtk6-devel` |
| **NixOS** | Add `gtk4` and `webkitgtk_6_0` to your environment |

### Step 2: Clone the Repository

```bash
git clone -b v3-alpha https://github.com/wailsapp/wails.git
cd wails/v3
```

### Step 3: Verify Installation

```bash
go install ./cmd/wails3
wails3 doctor
```

You should see both GTK3 (required) and GTK4 (experimental/optional) listed.

### Step 4: Run the Examples with GTK4

Browse the examples in `v3/examples/` and run them with the GTK4 tag:

```bash
# List available examples
ls examples/

# Run an example with GTK4
cd examples/menu
go run -tags gtk4 .

# Or build it
go build -tags gtk4 .
./menu
```

**Recommended examples to test:**
- `examples/menu` - Tests menu functionality
- `examples/dialogs` - Tests file/message dialogs  
- `examples/drag-n-drop` - Tests drag and drop
- `examples/window` - Tests window management
- `examples/events` - Tests event handling
- `examples/clipboard` - Tests clipboard operations

---

## What We Need You To Test

### 🔍 Test 1: Wails Doctor Output

Run `wails3 doctor` and report:
- [ ] Does it correctly detect your GTK3 packages as installed?
- [ ] Does it correctly detect your GTK4 packages (if installed)?
- [ ] Are the package names correct for your distro?

**If doctor shows wrong package names, please tell us:**
- Your distribution and version
- Your package manager (apt, dnf, pacman, etc.)
- The correct package names for your system

### 🪟 Test 2: Window Management

- [ ] Window opens correctly
- [ ] Window resizing works
- [ ] Window minimize/maximize/restore works
- [ ] Window close works
- [ ] Fullscreen toggle works
- [ ] Window dragging works (click and drag title bar area)

### 📋 Test 3: Menus

- [ ] Application menu bar displays
- [ ] Menu items are clickable
- [ ] Keyboard accelerators work (Ctrl+Q, etc.)
- [ ] Checkboxes in menus work
- [ ] Radio buttons in menus work
- [ ] Submenus work

### 📁 Test 4: Dialogs

- [ ] File Open dialog works
- [ ] File Save dialog works
- [ ] Folder selection dialog works
- [ ] Message/Alert dialogs work

### 🖱️ Test 5: Drag and Drop

- [ ] Dragging files into the window works
- [ ] Drop events are received correctly

### 📊 Test 6: Performance

Compare GTK3 vs GTK4 builds:
- [ ] App startup time
- [ ] UI responsiveness
- [ ] Scrolling smoothness
- [ ] Animation performance

### 🖥️ Test 7: Display

- [ ] Correct rendering on your display
- [ ] HiDPI/scaling works correctly
- [ ] Multiple monitors work

---

## How to Report Your Results

### Please include this info:

```
## System Info
- **Distro**: (e.g., Ubuntu 24.04, Fedora 40, Arch)
- **Package Manager**: (apt, dnf, pacman, zypper, emerge, eopkg, nix)
- **Desktop Environment**: (GNOME, KDE, XFCE, Sway, etc.)
- **Window Manager**: (Mutter, KWin, Sway, i3, etc.)
- **Display Server**: Wayland / X11
- **GTK4 Version**: `pkg-config --modversion gtk4`
- **WebKitGTK Version**: `pkg-config --modversion webkitgtk-6.0`

## Test Results
- Doctor output: ✅ / ❌ / ⚠️
- Window management: ✅ / ❌ / ⚠️
- Menus: ✅ / ❌ / ⚠️
- Dialogs: ✅ / ❌ / ⚠️
- Drag and drop: ✅ / ❌ / ⚠️
- Performance: Better / Same / Worse than GTK3
- Display/scaling: ✅ / ❌ / ⚠️

## Details
[Any specific issues, error messages, or observations]
```

---

## Reporting Bugs

**Please use sub-issues** to report specific bugs. This keeps everything organized under this parent issue.

To create a sub-issue:
1. Click "Create sub-issue" below
2. Use `[GTK4]` prefix in the title (e.g., `[GTK4] Menu accelerators not working on KDE Wayland`)
3. Include your system info and steps to reproduce

---

## Contributing Fixes

PRs welcome! Please:
1. Target the `v3-alpha` branch
2. Test with both default (GTK3) and `-tags gtk4` builds
3. Reference this issue in your PR

---

## Known Limitations

| Limitation | Reason |
|------------|--------|
| Window positioning on Wayland | Wayland protocol doesn't allow arbitrary positioning |
| `ShowHiddenFiles()` in file dialogs | GTK4 uses portal-based dialogs controlled by DE |
| `CanCreateDirectories()` | Same as above - portal controls this |
| X11 performance may vary | GTK4 is optimized primarily for Wayland |

## Related

- Original feature request: #3193
- Implementation tracker: See `IMPLEMENTATION.md` in repo
- Pull Request: #4958

---

**Thank you for helping test GTK4 support!** Your feedback directly shapes whether this becomes the default in a future release.
